apk_save_hint: Choose where to save the APK.
asset_exists: An asset with this name already exists in this category.
doc_act_create_obj: create rectangle, text, sprite, circle, line
doc_act_emit: call your own event with data (payload)
doc_act_flow: branching and loops (with nested blocks inside)
doc_act_info: See the full list of actions in the editor palette ('+' button). Each action has field hints.
doc_act_sound_code:
PlaySound: coin_sound, volume: 0.8, loop: false
StopSound: coin_sound
SetSoundVolume: music, volume: 50
doc_act_tweens_code:
TweenPosition: player → x: 400, y: 300, time: 1.0, ease: out
TweenOpacity: fade_out → value: 0, time: 0.5
TweenScale: bounce → percent: 150, time: 0.3
doc_actions_p: An action is a command. They execute in order from top to bottom inside an event.
doc_android_back_p: Android 'Back' button generates 'back' event. Handle it to show pause menu or save game. By default — exit app.
doc_android_orient_p: auto — sensor decides. portrait — vertical only. landscape — horizontal only. Changed by 'Orientation' block or in project settings.
doc_android_perms_p: Android requires explicit permissions for files, camera, microphone. Add them in project settings. READ_MEDIA_* needed for importing resources.
doc_android_storage_p: On Android 10+ direct file access is limited. Gyro Engine uses Storage Access Framework — system file picker dialog. Projects are stored in app's private folder.
doc_build_appname: app name visible to the user
doc_build_keystore_p: Keystore is a digital key file for signing APK. Without it, Android won't install the app.
doc_build_keystore_warning: Keystore is required for APK signing. Create it via keytool or import an existing one.
doc_build_p: Gyro Engine can build a ready APK right on the phone. You need project settings and a keystore.
doc_build_tip: Use the same keystore for all app versions, otherwise updates won't install.
doc_cam_follow_code:
CameraFollow: player, smooth: 5
# Camera will smoothly chase the player
doc_cam_follow_p: Camera smoothly follows an object. smooth — follow speed (more = sharper).
doc_cam_parallax_analogy: Like in a train: nearby posts flash fast, distant mountains — slowly. x=100 — like background, x=0 — glued to camera.
doc_cam_parallax_p: A parallax layer moves slower than the camera, creating a depth illusion.
doc_cam_pos_p: Hard-sets camera position at x, y coordinates.
doc_camera_p: Camera follows objects and creates parallax effect.
doc_cond_always_p: Always true. Used when you just need to group actions without a filter.
doc_cond_payload_code:
Event: collide
  Condition: PayloadEquals a = player
  └─ AddToVariable: score += 10
doc_cond_payload_p: Check event data. For example, in collide payload contains a and b — names of collided objects.
doc_cond_tip: You can combine multiple conditions — they all work as logical AND.
doc_cond_var_code:
Event: update
  Condition: VariableGreaterThan hp > 0
  └─ SetVisible: player, on: true

  Condition: VariableEquals hp = 0
  └─ EmitEvent: game_over
doc_cond_var_p: VariableEquals — variable equals value. VariableGreaterThan — greater. Numbers, text, booleans are supported.
doc_conditions_analogy: A condition is like a guard at the door. He checks the pass (condition) and only lets through those who are OK.
doc_conditions_p: Conditions filter events. A rule fires only if ALL conditions are true.
doc_debug_flow_p: If blocks don't execute: 1) Check event name (ready, tap, custom). 2) Check conditions — are all true. 3) Add Print before each block.
doc_debug_log_p: Enable 'Test log' in app settings to see Print output. Disable before release — it saves resources.
doc_debug_p: Tools for finding bugs and answers to common questions.
doc_debug_perf_p: If game lags: 1) Remove extra blocks in 'Every frame'. 2) Use tags instead of iterating objects. 3) Limit particles count.
doc_debug_print_code:
# Check if event fired
ready → Print: "Game started!"

# Check variable value
update → Print: "HP = " + $var.hp
doc_debug_print_p: Main debugging tool. Outputs text to the log at the bottom of the screen when running the game. Use to check variable values and block execution order.
doc_ev_app_p: back — Android 'Back' button. app_paused — app minimized. app_resumed — returning to the app.
doc_ev_collide_code:
Event: collide
  Condition: PayloadEquals a = player
  └─ AddToVariable: score += 10
  └─ PlaySound: coin
doc_ev_collide_p: collide — start of collision between two physics bodies. collide_end — end. In payload: a, b — object names.
doc_ev_custom_code:
Script A:
  EmitEvent: game_over

Script B:
  Event: custom (name: game_over)
    └─ Print: Game Over!
doc_ev_custom_p: custom — any event you call via EmitEvent. func — creating a function (also called via EmitEvent).
doc_ev_data_p: var_changed — variable changed (payload: name, old, new). widget_changed — widget value changed. http_done — HTTP response arrived (payload: status, body).
doc_ev_drag_p: Fires when finger/mouse moves. In payload: x, y, dx, dy (offset).
doc_ev_input_p: Detailed input event. In payload: type (key/mouse_button/touch), keycode, button, x, y, text.
doc_ev_ready_code:
Event: ready
  └─ SetVariable: score = 0
  └─ CreateObject: player
doc_ev_ready_p: Fires once when the scene is loaded. Perfect for creating objects and initialization.
doc_ev_tap_code:
Event: tap
  └─ CreateObject: bullet
        x: $payload.x
        y: $payload.y
doc_ev_tap_p: Fires on screen touch. x, y coordinates come in payload.
doc_ev_timer_p: Fires when a timer expires. In payload: name — timer name. Timers are created with StartTimer action.
doc_ev_touch_p: Fires when touching a specific object (not the screen!). Requires an object with a physics body (SetSolid or SetSensor).
doc_ev_update_p: Fires ~60 times per second. Use for smooth movement, checks, animations. Caution: heavy logic here slows down the game.
doc_events_analogy: An event is like a doorbell. When someone rings (event), you open the door (actions). Without the ring — the door stays closed.
doc_events_p: An event is a trigger. When it happens, all actions inside the rule are executed.
doc_faq_apk:
Q: Why APK doesn't install?
A: 1) Check keystore — alias and password. 2) Make sure package name is unique (com.your.name). 3) Check if old version with different key is installed.
doc_faq_collision:
Q: Why object passes through wall?
A: 1) Both objects must have 'Solid object' = true. 2) Check sizes are correct after changing via 'Set object size'. 3) Make sure velocity isn't too high.
doc_faq_perf:
Q: How many objects can be created?
A: On mobile devices, 200-300 active objects is comfortable. Use tags for mass operations and avoid heavy logic in 'Every frame'.
doc_faq_sound:
Q: Why sound doesn't play?
A: 1) Check resource is added to 'Sound' category. 2) Name in block must match resource name. 3) Check volume (not 0).
doc_faq_svg:
Q: Why SVG doesn't work as APK icon?
A: Android doesn't support SVG as icon. Use PNG, JPG or WebP. SVG works only for sprites.
doc_faq_var:
Q: Why variable doesn't change?
A: 1) Check name — it's case sensitive. 2) Use 'Variable =' to write. 3) Check block executes (add Print).
doc_files_p: Save data locally and work with the network via HTTP.
doc_files_save: simple save by key (automatically in JSON)
doc_for_whom_p: For beginners who want to create their first game without learning programming. For those who value prototyping speed. For mobile developers.
doc_import_backup_p: Gyro Engine automatically creates project backups (configurable in app settings: off / 1-60 min). Stored in .backups folder next to project. Maximum 3 backups. Restore via 'Backups' button in project hub.
doc_import_export_p: In project hub tap 'Export'. Choose save location. .gyroproj file contains everything needed to open on another device.
doc_import_formats_p: .tres — native Godot format. Stores project as resource. .gyroproj — Gyro Engine archive, contains project + all resources (sprites, sounds). Ideal for sharing.
doc_import_import_p: In project manager tap import button (down arrow). Choose .gyroproj or .tres file. Project will appear in list.
doc_import_p: How to save, transfer and restore projects.
doc_import_warning: Warning: when deleting project, backups are also deleted. Export important projects to .gyroproj!
doc_interface_info: All changes are saved automatically. Backups are created on schedule (configurable in App Settings).
doc_interface_p: Gyro Engine consists of several screens. Each handles its own task.
doc_intro_analogy: Imagine you're building Lego. Each block is a brick of logic. By connecting them, you create game behavior. An event is 'when...', a condition is 'if...', an action is 'do...'.
doc_intro_b1: Create 2D games: platformers, arcades, puzzles, clickers
doc_intro_b4: Build APK right on the phone
doc_intro_info: Gyro Engine runs on Godot 4.7 and exports to Android APK. All projects are stored locally on the device.
doc_intro_p1: Gyro Engine is a visual engine for creating 2D games without writing code. Instead of text, you assemble logic from colored blocks, like a constructor.
doc_multitouch_p: Gyro Engine handles one touch at a time (first). For multitouch use 'Input' event with type='touch' — it has touch index. But most games use single touch.
doc_obj_hierarchy_analogy: Like folders on a computer. A file inside a folder has the path folder/file. Similarly, an object inside a group inherits its coordinates.
doc_obj_hierarchy_p: Objects can be nested in groups (CreateGroup + AddToGroup). Child position is relative to parent.
doc_obj_props_p: Via SetNodeProperty you can change any properties directly:
doc_obj_tip: Object name is unique. If you create an object with an existing name, the old one will be deleted.
doc_objects_p: Objects are visible entities on the scene. Each has a name, position, size, and properties.
doc_part_code:
CreateParticles: snow_fx
  preset: snow
  x: 240, y: 0

SetParticlesParam: snow_fx
  param: speed, value: 200
doc_particles_p: Particle systems for effects: snow, rain, fire, sparks, confetti.
doc_perf_limits_p: Comfortable limits on mobile: 200-300 objects, 50-100 particles, 10-20 sounds simultaneously. More — possible FPS drop.
doc_perf_measure_p: Use Print with timestamps to measure block execution time. If block takes >16ms — it's too heavy (target is 60 FPS = 16ms per frame).
doc_perf_tips_p: 1) Avoid heavy logic in 'Every frame' — use timers. 2) Use tags for mass operations. 3) Delete unused objects. 4) Limit particles. 5) Use sprites instead of complex polygons.
doc_phys_code1:
# Player jump
Event: tap
  Condition: PayloadEquals a = player
  └─ AddVelocity: player, y: -700

# Gravity
ready → SetGravity: player, value: 1500
doc_phys_coll_code:
Event: collide
  Condition: PayloadEquals a = player
  └─ PlaySound: hit
  └─ AddToVariable: hp -= 10
doc_phys_coll_p: To catch collisions, both objects must have physics bodies. collide/collide_end events come with payload {a, b}.
doc_phys_drag_p: Make an object draggable: SetDraggable: player, on: true. The object will follow the finger.
doc_phys_sensor: sensor — registers collisions but doesn't push
doc_phys_warning: Physics works only in RigidBody2D. Static objects (SetSolid) don't move themselves but can collide.
doc_physics_p: Gyro Engine uses Godot physics (RigidBody2D, StaticBody2D, Area2D) under the hood. You control it visually.
doc_qs_code1:
Event: ready
  └─ Action: CreateObject
        name: obj1
        type: rect
        x: 200, y: 400
        w: 80, h: 80
        color: #ff8800
doc_qs_step1: Open Project Manager → tap '+' → enter name → 'Create'.
doc_qs_step2: In project hub open 'Structure' → '+' → 'Script' → name it 'Main'.
doc_qs_step4: Inside the event tap '+' → 'Objects' → 'Create object'. An orange rectangle will appear.
doc_qs_step5: Add event 'Screen tap' → action 'Impulse' with Y = -700. Don't forget to make the object solid: action 'Solid object' = true.
doc_qs_tip: Tap ▶ at the bottom to run the game. The '✕' button in the top right corner stops the test.
doc_quickstart_p: In 5 minutes you'll create your first game: a square that jumps on tap.
doc_res_folders_p: Resources can be organized in folders inside each category. For example: sprite/characters/hero.png.
doc_res_info: SVG is not supported as APK icon — only PNG/JPG/WebP. For sprites SVG works.
doc_res_usage_code:
CreateObject: hero
  type: sprite
  texture: hero_walk  ← resource name from the list
doc_res_usage_p: In actions (CreateObject, PlaySound) choose a resource from the dropdown. Gyro Engine will find it by name or ID.
doc_resources_p: Resources are files you import into the project: images, sounds, fonts.
doc_screen_editor_p: The heart of Gyro Engine. Here you assemble logic from events, conditions, and actions. Drag blocks, collapse, copy.
doc_screen_home_p: Entry point. Three buttons: Manager, Documentation, Settings.
doc_screen_hub_p: Control center of the opened project. Buttons: Structure, Resources, Settings, Backups, Export, Play.
doc_screen_manager_p: List of all your projects. Here you can:
doc_screen_resources_p: Sprites, sounds, fonts, videos. Organized by category. Drag files between folders.
doc_screen_structure_p: Tree of folders and scripts. Each script is a set of rules (events). Double-tap a script to open the block editor.
doc_sound_formats_p: MP3 — compressed, small size, good for music. OGG — open format, good quality, ideal for sounds. WAV — uncompressed, large size, used for short effects.
doc_sound_loop_p: loop: true makes sound infinite. Good for background music. Stop it with 'Stop sound' block.
doc_sound_multi_p: Each sound plays in its own AudioStreamPlayer. You can play music and effects simultaneously. Use different names for different sounds.
doc_sound_p: Gyro Engine supports MP3, OGG and WAV. Sounds are loaded via Resources menu and used with 'Play sound' block.
doc_sound_tip: Tip: use OGG for effects (fast loading) and MP3 for music (small size).
doc_sound_volume_p: volume from 0.0 to 1.0 (or 0-100 in 'Sound volume'). Can be changed in real time.
doc_tab_json_p: You can load a table from a JSON string:
doc_tab_loops_p: ForEachTable — iterate through all table elements. LoopRange — loop from N to M with step.
doc_tables_p: Variables of type table are dictionaries (key→value) or arrays (index→value).
doc_tags_analogy: Like colored stickers on boxes. 'Red' — fragile, 'blue' — glass. You can grab all 'red' boxes at once.
doc_tags_code:
# Mark all enemies
ready → AddTag: enemy1, tag: enemy
ready → AddTag: enemy2, tag: enemy

# Kill all enemies
Event: custom (bomb_exploded)
  └─ DeleteByTag: enemy
doc_tags_p: Tags are a way to mark objects for mass operations. One object can have multiple tags.
doc_tags_tip: Tags persist between events. If an object is deleted, its tags are cleared automatically.
doc_vars_expr_p: You can write formulas in value fields. The expression editor opens by tapping the field:
doc_vars_p: Variables store data between events. Available in all project scripts.
doc_vars_syntax_p: In action and condition fields use $var.name to read a variable, $payload.key for event data:
doc_vars_warning: Variable names: only Latin, digits and _, up to 32 chars. Cannot start with a digit.
doc_wid_events_p: When a widget value changes, widget_changed event fires. In payload come name and value.
doc_wid_info: Widgets live on the UI layer above the scene. They don't participate in physics.
doc_wid_input_code:
CreateInput: name_field
  x: 100, y: 200, w: 240
  text: "Your name"
  multiline: false
  secret: false
doc_wid_input_p: Creates a text field. Supports multiline and password modes.
doc_wid_slider_p: Creates a slider (horizontal or vertical). Value from 0 to 100.
doc_wid_toggle_p: Creates a toggle (checkbox). State is true/false.
doc_widgets_p: Widgets are interactive UI elements: input field, slider, toggle.

doc_build_keystore_alt: Or use an online keystore generator. Then import the .p12 in project settings.
doc_anchors_p: Anchors attach an object to a screen point. When the screen resizes, the object stays in place.
doc_anchors_analogy: Like buttons in a mobile app: 'Back' is always bottom-left, 'Menu' — top-right. They don't move when you rotate the screen.
doc_anchors_set_p: Attaches an object to a screen point. x, y set the offset from that point.
doc_anchors_set_code:
SetAnchor: player, anchor: bl
MoveNode: player, x: 20, y: -20
# Player 20px from bottom-left corner
doc_anchors_offset_p: After SetAnchor use MoveNode for offset. Offset is preserved on screen resize.
doc_anchors_offset_code:
SetAnchor: score_label, anchor: tr
MoveNode: score_label, x: -10, y: 10
# Score in top-right with padding
doc_anchors_warning: If you change position via SetNodeProperty position — anchor resets. Use MoveNode.
doc_groups_p: A group is a container for other objects. All children move together with the group.
doc_groups_analogy: Like a folder on a computer. Move the folder — all files inside move with it.
doc_groups_create_code: CreateGroup: ui_layer, x: 0, y: 0, w: 480, h: 720
doc_groups_add_p: Puts an object inside a group. Object coordinates become relative.
doc_groups_add_code:
CreateGroup: ui_layer
CreateObject: button, x: 100, y: 100
AddToGroup: button, group: ui_layer
# Now button is inside ui_layer
doc_groups_relative_p: After AddToGroup, object position is relative to group. Group at (100, 50), object at (10, 10) → global (110, 60).
doc_groups_warning: Groups are not tags! Groups are physical hierarchy, tags are logical labels.
doc_sprite_anim_p: Animation from a spritesheet — a single image with multiple frames.
doc_sprite_anim_create_p: Creates an animated object from a spritesheet.
doc_sprite_anim_create_code:
CreateSpriteAnim: hero
sprite: hero_walk
frame_w: 32, frame_h: 32
count: 8, fps: 12
anim: walk
x: 100, y: 200
doc_sprite_anim_frame_size: size of one frame in pixels
doc_sprite_anim_control_p: Control playback: switch frames, start and stop.
doc_sprite_anim_control_code:
SetFrame: hero, frame: 3
PlayAnimation: hero, animation: attack
StopAnimation: hero
doc_sprite_anim_tip: Frames in spritesheets go left-to-right, top-to-bottom. 8 frames 32×32 in 256×32 sheet — all in one row.
doc_shapes_p: Circle and Line — basic graphic primitives.
doc_shapes_circle_p: Creates a circle with fill and border.
doc_shapes_circle_code:
CreateCircle: coin
radius: 25
color: #ffcc00
border_w: 3
border_color: #aa8800
x: 200, y: 300
doc_shapes_line_p: Creates a line between two points.
doc_shapes_line_code:
CreateLine: laser
x: 100, y: 100
x2: 400, y2: 300
color: #ff0000
width: 4
doc_shapes_physics_p: Circles and lines automatically get physics bodies. Circle — circular shape, line — capsule. You can use SetSolid / SetSensor.
doc_styles_p: Gradients, borders, and corner radius for visual design.
doc_styles_gradient_p: Fills an object with a two-color gradient.
doc_styles_gradient_code:
SetGradient: panel
mode: linear
color1: #ff8800
color2: #0000ff
doc_styles_border_p: Adds a border around an object.
doc_styles_corner_code:
CreateObject: btn, type: rect, w: 200, h: 60
SetCornerRadius: btn, radius: 15
doc_transforms_p: Pivot point, face object, custom metadata.
doc_transforms_pivot_p: Changes the rotation pivot. Default is center. (0,0) — top-left, (100,100) — bottom-right.
doc_transforms_pivot_code:
SetPivot: door, x: 0, y: 50
# Door rotates around left edge (like a real door)
doc_transforms_face_p: Rotates object to face the target.
doc_transforms_meta_p: Stores custom data on an object. Read via SetObjectMeta / use in conditions.
doc_transforms_meta_code:
SetObjectMeta: chest, key: gold, value: 100
SetObjectMeta: chest, key: opened, value: false
doc_transforms_meta_tip: Metadata lives only while the object exists. Lost on deletion.
doc_spawn_p: Spawn creates an object from a ready .tscn scene (e.g. from another project).
doc_spawn_action_p: Creates a scene instance in the game.
doc_spawn_action_code:
Spawn: enemy_scene
parent: enemies_group
x: 300, y: 100
variable: last_enemy
doc_spawn_var: variable to reference the created object
doc_spawn_warning: Scene must be imported to resources as 'other'. Path is specified as resource name.
doc_tweens_p: Tween is a smooth property change over a given time.
doc_tweens_analogy: Like an elevator: you set the floor (target) and speed (time). It moves smoothly, not teleports.
doc_tweens_pos_p: Smoothly moves object to a point over time.
doc_tweens_pos_code:
TweenPosition: player
x: 400, y: 300
time: 1.0
ease: out
doc_tweens_other_p: Scale, rotation, and opacity follow the same rules.
doc_tweens_other_code:
TweenScale: icon, percent: 150, time: 0.3
TweenRotation: arrow, angle: 360, time: 2.0
TweenOpacity: fade, value: 0, time: 0.5
doc_tweens_stop_p: Stops all tweens of an object.
doc_tweens_tip: A new tween on the same object kills the previous one. Use StopTween before a new one if you need control.
doc_draggable_p: Object can be dragged by finger/mouse.
doc_draggable_set_p: Enables dragging mode for an object.
doc_draggable_events_p: Drag event fires when finger moves. In payload: x, y, dx, dy.
doc_draggable_tip: Dragging works only for objects with a physics body (SetSolid or SetSensor).
doc_system_actions_p: Actions for system integration: notifications, links, clipboard.
doc_system_toast_p: Shows a popup notification for 2 seconds.
doc_system_url_p: Opens a link in the browser.
doc_system_clipboard_code:
Clipboard: mode: set, text: "Copied!"
Clipboard: mode: get, variable: clipboard_text
doc_system_seed_p: Sets seed for rand(). Same seed = same sequence.
doc_system_seed_code:
RandomSeed: 42
# Now rand(0, 100) always gives the same numbers
doc_system_orient_p: Changes screen orientation: auto / portrait / landscape.
doc_custom_events_p: Create your own events to communicate between scripts.
doc_custom_payload_p: JSON object with event data. Read via $payload.key.
doc_custom_payload_code:
# Script A:
EmitEvent: damage, payload: {"amount": 25}

# Script B:
Event: custom (name: damage)
AddToVariable: hp, amount: -$payload.amount
doc_custom_func_p: func is a custom event called via EmitEvent. Differs from custom only semantically.
doc_custom_func_code:
# Declaration:
Event: func (name: take_damage)
AddToVariable: hp, amount: -$payload.amount

# Call:
EmitEvent: take_damage, payload: {"amount": 10}
doc_custom_warning: If two scripts have an event with the same name — both fire. Use unique names.
doc_expressions_p: You can write formulas in value fields. Tap a field to open the expression editor.
doc_expressions_syntax_p: Use $var.name to read variables and $payload.key for event data.
doc_expressions_examples_code:
# Random 0 to 100
rand(0, 100)

# Clamp value
clamp($var.hp, 0, 100)

# Round
round($var.score / 10) * 10

# Text length
len($var.name)
doc_layout_mode_p: Visual editor for precise object positioning on screen.
doc_layout_mode_how_p: Run test ▶ → tap the grid icon top-right. Layout mode opens.
doc_layout_mode_b2: Objects snap to screen center and edges
doc_layout_mode_b3: Tap a dot (•) around an object — apply anchor
doc_layout_mode_aspects_p: Shows how the game looks on screens with different aspect ratios. Objects outside the frame will be cropped.
doc_layout_mode_warning: Game is paused in layout mode. MoveNode/Tween blocks in events reset anchors.
doc_advanced_physics_p: Details of the physics engine under the hood.
doc_adv_phys_static: static body (wall, floor) — doesn't move but collides
doc_adv_phys_global_p: Pause freezes all bodies. Global gravity applies to all objects at once.
doc_adv_phys_collision_p: To catch collisions, both objects must have physics bodies. collide/collide_end events come with payload {a, b}.
doc_adv_phys_collision_code:
Event: collide
Condition: PayloadEquals a = player
  PlaySound: hit
  AddToVariable: hp, amount: -10
doc_adv_phys_shapes_p: Collision shape is auto-created from visual: Sprite2D → rectangle, Circle → circle, Line → capsule. On resize — shape updates.
doc_adv_files_op_p: FileOp performs file operations: delete, mkdir, copy, move.
doc_adv_files_op_code:
FileOp: op: mkdir, path1: user://saves
FileOp: op: copy, path1: user://a.txt, path2: user://b.txt
FileOp: op: delete, path1: user://old.txt
doc_adv_files_http_p: Sends an HTTP request. Result — in variable or http_done event.
doc_adv_files_http_code:
HttpRequest:
url: https://api.example.com/data
method: GET
variable: response

# Or catch event:
Event: http_done
Print: "Status: " + $payload.status
doc_adv_files_save_p: Simple key-value save. Data stored as JSON inside the project.
doc_adv_files_save_code:
SaveValue: key: high_score, value: $var.score
LoadValue: key: high_score, variable: best
doc_adv_files_save_tip: SaveValue/LoadValue — for simple saves. For complex data use ReadFile/WriteFile with JSON.
doc_backups_p: Gyro Engine automatically creates project backups.
doc_backups_auto_p: Configured in app settings: off / 1 / 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 minutes. Stored in .backups folder next to project. Maximum 3 copies.
doc_backups_manual_p: In project hub tap 'Backups' → 'Create backup'. Copy is made immediately.
doc_backups_restore_p: In the same menu pick a copy by date — project restores from it.
doc_backups_warning: When deleting a project, backups are also deleted! Export important projects to .gyroproj.
about_description: A visual engine for creating games and apps without code. Build logic from blocks, add objects, and run your project right on your phone.
